mission.title: Install and Configure Linode Kubernetes Engine (LKE)
mission.description: Linode Kubernetes Engine (LKE) is a managed Kubernetes service that simplifies the deployment and management of Kubernetes clusters on Linode's infrastructure. It is ideal for users looking for a hassle-free way to run Kubernetes without managing the underlying hardware. Key trade-offs include limited customization compared to self-managed solutions and potential cost implications based on resource usage.

steps.title: Install the Linode CLI
steps.description:
This step installs the Linode CLI, which is necessary for managing your Linode resources from the command line.

```bash

curl -O https://linode.com/cli/linode-cli-1.22.0.tar.gz

tar -xzf linode-cli-1.22.0.tar.gz

sudo mv linode-cli /usr/local/bin/

linode-cli configure

```

> Download the Linode CLI tarball.
> Extract the downloaded tarball.
> Move the CLI to a directory in your PATH.
> Configure the CLI with your Linode API token.

steps.title: Create a Kubernetes Cluster
steps.description:
This step creates a new Kubernetes cluster on Linode with the specified version and node count.

```bash

linode-cli k8s cluster-create --label my-k8s-cluster --region us-east --k8s-version 1.30 --node-count 3

```

> Create a cluster with 3 nodes in the US East region.

steps.title: Set Up Kubeconfig
steps.description:
This step configures your kubeconfig file to interact with the newly created Kubernetes cluster.

```bash

linode-cli k8s kubeconfig-view my-k8s-cluster > ~/.kube/config

```

> Save the kubeconfig to your local machine.

steps.title: Verify Cluster Nodes
steps.description:
This step checks the status of the nodes in your Kubernetes cluster to ensure they are ready.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> List all nodes and their statuses.

steps.title: Post-Install Configuration
steps.description:
This step sets up essential features like autoscaling and monitoring for your cluster.

```bash

kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/linode/linode-cloud-controller-manager/v0.9.6/deploy/ccm-linode-template.yaml

kubectl create clusterrolebinding ccm-linode --clusterrole=cluster-admin --serviceaccount=kube-system:ccm-linode

```

> Deploy the Linode Cloud Controller Manager.
> Bind the necessary roles for the Cloud Controller Manager.

uninstall.title: Delete the Kubernetes Cluster
uninstall.description:
This step will remove the Kubernetes cluster and all associated resources. Be aware that this will result in data loss.

```bash

linode-cli k8s cluster-delete my-k8s-cluster

```

> Delete the cluster and all its resources.

uninstall.title: Remove the Linode CLI
uninstall.description:
This step removes the Linode CLI from your system.

```bash

sudo rm /usr/local/bin/linode-cli

```

> Remove the CLI binary.

upgrade.title: Upgrade the Kubernetes Cluster
upgrade.description:
Before upgrading, ensure you backup your data and configurations. This step will upgrade your cluster to the latest version.

```bash

kubectl get nodes -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.status.conditions[] | select(.type=="Ready") | .status=="False")'

linode-cli k8s cluster-update my-k8s-cluster --k8s-version 1.30

kubectl get nodes

```

> Check for any nodes that are not ready before upgrading.
> Upgrade the cluster to version 1.30.
> Verify that all nodes are ready after the upgrade.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Unable to connect to the server: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that your kubeconfig is not correctly set up or the cluster is not reachable.

**Fix:**
Re-run the kubeconfig setup command: linode-cli k8s kubeconfig-view my-k8s-cluster > ~/.kube/config

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Insufficient nodes available to fulfill the request'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This means that there are not enough nodes in the cluster to accommodate the requested resources.

**Fix:**
Increase the node count using: linode-cli k8s cluster-update my-k8s-cluster --node-count <new-count>

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Failed to create service: Service is invalid'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that the service definition has invalid parameters.

**Fix:**
Check the service configuration and ensure all required fields are correctly defined.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Node not found'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This usually means that the node has been deleted or is not in the expected state.

**Fix:**
Check the status of the nodes with: kubectl get nodes and recreate any missing nodes.
